language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Bonjour! This is my son Pierre, you can call me Papa. We live in Champagne, France where my family grows grapes to make wine.
Pierre is an early bird, he loves going outside as soon as the sun comes up. He just asked me why the sun has to go away every day and why it can't stay daytime forever.
Well Pierre, the sun goes away when night comes. The sun will return the next day. Believe it or not, it is not the sun that is moving, it is the Earth!
Thats funny, I don't feel like I'm moving!

It is not as simple as just day and night. There are also moments in the day in between. When the sun rises, it is morning. When the sun is at it's highest, it is noon.
When the sun goes down and starts to disappear, it is sunset. Finally, when the sun is gone, it is night again.
Look at the pictures and decide what time of day it is.

To understand day and night, we need to know something about our planet and the sun. The sun is the centre of our Solar System. It shines light on all the planets.

Earth is one of the planets that moves around the sun. The circle it makes is called the orbit. Earth orbits the sun. Do you see the Moon? It is the small circle going around the Earth. The Moon orbits Earth and Earth orbits the sun!
Can you put the sun, the Moon, and the Earth in the right place in the Solar System?

dialog.text: To understand day and night, we need to know something about our planet and the sun. The sun is the centre of our Solar System. It shines light on all the planets.

Earth is one of the planets that moves around the sun. The circle it makes is called the orbit. Earth orbits the sun. Do you see the Moon? It is the small circle going around the Earth. The Moon orbits Earth and Earth orbits the sun!
Can you put the sun, the Moon, and the Earth in the right place in the Solar System?

Great work!
Here is the Earth. Now, as I mentioned before, it is not the sun that moves, it is the Earth!
The Earth has something called an axis. Imagine a stick put through the Earth. The Earth spins around that axis. And as it spins, the sun shines on different areas of the Earth.
The side of the Earth that faces the sun is experiencing daytime. The side away from the sun is experiencing nighttime.
As we move from the sunny side to the dark, this is sunset. As we move from the dark to the sunny side, this is Morning.
Let's see what you've learned about day and night.
